Typically, FOG is not used in its raw form—industries purchase purified material from rendering plants. This analysis excludes edible animal fats, namely lard and edible tallow. • Wet organic waste comprises animal manure, wastewater sludge, and food waste (also an MSW material). As their collective name implies, these resources have high moisture content and thus are suitable for conversion processes able to handle this type of feedstock, such as anaerobic digestion (AD). Data for animal manure and wastewater sludge was obtained from Milbrandt et al. 2018. Using EPA’s MSW composition data (2020), we estimated the amount of each material (including food waste) generated in each state by multiplying total MSW generation by the material’s percentage share. Then calculate the state’s per capita generation rate and apply it to each ZIP code’s population to estimate the quantity of each material (including food waste) generated by ZIP code. • MSW is waste collected from residential, institutional, commercial, and industrial entities. It is assumed that paper/cardboard, plastics, textiles, rubber, yard trimmings, and clean wood would be converted to SAF. As described above for food waste, we used EPA’s MSW composition data (2020) to estimate the amount of each material generated in each state by multiplying total MSW generation by the material’s percentage share. Then calculate the state’s per capita generation rate and apply it to each ZIP code’s population to estimate the quantity of each material generated by ZIP code. • Lignocellulosic biomass (woody biomass and crop residues). Woody biomass includes logging residues and other removable material left after carrying out forestry operations and site conversions (such as fire reduction thinnings, other forest waste, and small- diameter trees), primary mill or processing residues (materials generated at wood mills when round wood products are processed into primary wood products, including bark, chips, and sawdust), other forest processing waste, and orchard prunings. Crop residues in the region include corn stover and wheat straw. Data for woody biomass and crop residues by county was obtained from the US. DOE’s 2023 Billion Ton Study (DOE 2024). A biomass resource assessment was conducted to evaluate the regional availability of SAF feedstocks near selected airports in the Northeast. This analysis, performed by NLR, focused on 11 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) at www.nlr.gov/publications. examining resource availability within three geographic ranges: within 5 miles (for feedstocks that are typically not economically transportable in their raw form, such as wet organic waste) and within 50- and 100-mile radii of the selected airport locations. Depending on the location of the airport, these radii would be drawing in feedstock from neighboring states, including in some instances New York (Appendix A provides New York county data).
